goals.title: Ride the hook you bent
goals.critique: This is the third round of the wire line. It deals with last round's main fault: hanging on a line over the pond and riding it makes success loud, and the jolt at push-off means a hook that held still can fail in motion, so every ride is a quick, readable bet. The splash a body length from the far bank is a clip people would send. But the pitch is still two clauses plus a rule. Once the player learns how far to over-bend for each friend, the loop may shrink to one zip line ridden again and again. The road still rests on the unbuilt GPU rod solver with plasticity, creep and fatigue, and the playable peg-bend step with visible springback has to show that a few degrees read as feel before the ride means anything.

goals.title: Carve a boat from a log
goals.critique: This one is new and strong in the human's direction. A chip-by-chip carve that stays, buoyancy and roll taken from the hull's own mesh, and loading friends one by one make a slow, tense build-up with a loud ending, and the last friend rolling the boat over is a clip people would send. Reading a hull by eye is a real skill to learn, and the boat stays in the world as a way to the rock island. The weak spots: boat building and capsizing are familiar from sandbox and ship games, and adze carving may play as a slow, imprecise sculpt unless every cut shows its effect on the waterline before launch. Once one stable hull works there is little reason to carve another, and the far island is a single destination, so the long-term play is thin.

goals.title: Grind a lens from sea glass
goals.critique: This is round 12's lens again, but the rework answers its sharpest fault: the sun spot moving on the sand with every stroke removes blind sanding, and dropping the burning trick sharpens it into one striking payoff, the camera obscura in the dark cottage. That is the most novel image of all the rounds and the clearest showcase for the path tracer. But grinding is one material on one tool, a frame of lenses is a gallery rather than something the island stands on or uses, and once a sharp lens exists there is little to strive for, so play is likely to fade after a few lenses. Live caustics through a hand-ground surface that also read in the browser raster are still an unproven rendering bet, and the tracer film has to come first.
